name: Baltanás (Spain)
description: Horizontal tricolour of purple, white and purple with a broad white stripe, charged at the centre with the crowned arms of Baltanás (five castles in saltire on red, supported by two lions).
history: Baltanás adopted its arms and flag officially on 30 May 1996, published in the Boletín Oficial de Castilla y León on 20 May 1996; the flag bears the arms of the town at the centre. At official events the flag is escorted by the mace-bearers, an office centuries old held by three people in gala dress, whose costumes imitate the old Somatén, an armed civil police that escorted the flag and the Blessed Sacrament at the feast of Corpus Christi.
